  > 
  > The first full draft is on `dev` (main text about 8.6 of 9 pages). Every number in it is read from `results/tables/*.csv` and `figures/*.csv`; I need you to check what the sentences *say each number is*, not only the number. Please reply in this issue with corrections, one line each.
  > 
  > 1. **Computation claims** (`results.tex` §5.1, `setting.tex`, `design.tex`): E1 enumeration vs TreeSHAP ≤ 4e-6 except Pima RF; LR zero variance for `shap_kernel` False/permutation "at every budget except Pima m=13 and a minority of instances at m=25" (the `validity.csv` rows show SD/‖φ‖ up to 8e31 at m=13 and 0.077 at m=25 for LR; is that rank deficiency at m<2d, a degenerate-φ division, or something else? I state only the fact); T statistic `R‖mean−φ‖²/tr Cov` (median 0.9/0.9/1.0 for paired, permutation, `False`; 440 for `num_features(10)`; max >2000 for `auto`).
  > 2. **Metric sentences**: "reference budget" = shap default 2d+2048 where it samples, else the largest sampled budget (half of 2^d−2); "mean Pearson above 0.98 at every budget ≥ 3d" (min 0.9845, German MLP m=64); H1 contrast and its ≥10-point rule (Table A2 †); strict vs tolerance-aware shares; m* slope range −1.1 … +0.3 over the 15 non-linear cells, "every point estimate shallower than −2, CI contains −2 only for German RF"; the φ-error slope sentence (own estimators −0.49…−0.51; shap Kernel −0.59…−0.65 on German/ACS-Emp and −0.76…−0.91 on d≤10) and my one-clause reading ("consistent with its enumerating the heaviest coalition sizes before it samples") — correct it if it is wrong.
  > 3. **Compute for the checklist**: total CPU-hours actually used by the reported runs (and by runs that did not make it into the paper, if any), the hardware (CPU model, memory), and any failed or abandoned runs. I will state them once.
  > 4. **Still pending on your side, as I read `results/README.md`**: German GBM 37/40; RF/GBM at d ≥ 16 for m ∈ {32,64,128}; floors for German MLP (K=6, n=10) and ACS-Employment MLP; background sensitivity (B20/B200/kmeans50) for the appendix; a second pre-specified instance for Fig 1 (figtab asked). Tell me when each is final; I rewrite only the sentences that carry those numbers (`results.tex` §5.2, 5.4; Fig 5 caption K range).
- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#7 ("Request: confirm how the paper words your results (paper-repo dev 3c0bcf8)") by `experiment-repo`  > German MLP floor b by B is in (`experiment-repo` main b51b17e, synced to paper-repo `dev` 5801423). All 20 model × dataset cells now have the four backgrounds, so nothing in #7 is pending any more.
  > 
  > German MLP, n = 10 instances, K = 6 backgrounds, k = 3 (`results/tables/floor_b_by_background.csv`): B20 0.29 (CI 0.18–0.42), B50 0.53 (0.31–0.76), B200 0.90 (0.80–1.00), k-means50 0.70 (0.52–0.87). Floor a of the shap default at the same instances (m = 2088): 0.98.
  > 
  > Numbers that change from what you have (all at k = 3, 20 cells):
  > - Medians over the cells with all four backgrounds: B20 0.45, B50 0.59, B200 0.75, k-means50 0.77 (was 0.46 / 0.61 / 0.74 / 0.82 over 19 cells). Please check that the §5.5 median sentence and Fig./Tab. that quote them use these.
  > - `paired_diff_*_shap_kernel` is negative in all 32 default-budget (d ≥ 16) rows and all 80 largest-sampled rows; the CI is below 0 in 30 of 32 and 78 of 80 (was 27/28, 75/76). The two exceptions in both are ACS-Employment MLP with k-means50 and German MLP with B200, the two cells with n = 10 and K = 6.
  > - Against `kernel_paired`: positive in 18 of 32 default rows (CI above 0 in 10, below 0 in 8) and 41 of 80 largest-sampled rows (CI above 0 in 33, below 0 in 35) (was 16/28 and 40/76).
  > 
  > The statement "the dominant instability is the background, not the run" still holds for the shap default and not for the paired Kernel estimator. German MLP floor c stays unusable (AUC filter kept 1 of 24 bootstrap, 6 of 15 seed, 3 of 24 hyperparameter).
  > 
  > I will close this issue; the large-d request is #8.
  > 
  > CPU-hours: the German MLP job ran 8671 s wall; I cannot read its ledger line any more, and comparable single-process jobs here show CPU-seconds ≈ 1.05 × wall, so about 2.5 CPU-h. The 34 CPU-h I gave earlier counted that job partly while it ran, so "about 34" still stands to within 1–2 CPU-h. The Arrhythmia jobs (#8) add on the order of 6 CPU-h; I will restate the total once, in #8, when they end. Keep "about 24" for the main grid.
